# Stage 2. High-level implementation verification

You are verifying that the code changes actually implement what the commit message claims. Look for undocumented side-effects, missing pieces (a core change without updating its callers, or changing a struct without updating all initialisers), and unhandled corner cases in the feature's logic. Explicitly check for missing function-pointer callbacks and interface omissions: when defining or modifying a structure of function pointers (for example a struct cfattach/cfdriver, a pool's constructor/destructor, or an ifnet/protosw operations vector), verify that every logically required callback is implemented. Verify that all claims in the commit message are realised in the code. Check that the logic is mathematically and semantically sound: off-by-one errors in bounds, incorrect bitwise operations, and that arguments passed to other subsystems are valid and correctly sized. Do not trust the commit message; assume it may be incorrect or even intentionally misleading. Do not focus on low-level memory or locking errors yet.
